 Dated this the 8th day of October 2025
 Judgment

This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.770/2015 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kollam,
(the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 16/10/2017.
The sole respondent herein is the second respondent/insurer in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 23/10/2014 at about 06:30 p.m., while she was travelling in autorickshaw bearing registration no.KL-2R 9780 driven by the first respondent through the Titanium-Sasthamcotta road, the latter swerved the vehicle in a 2025:KER:74441 MACA NO. 831 OF 2020 rash and negligent manner, as a result of which she fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
A sum of 15,00,000/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.
3. The first respondent/owner-cum-driver of the offending vehicle filed written statement contending that he was having valid licence and that the vehicle was insured with the second respondent.
4. The second respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the existence of a valid policy in respect of the offending vehicle.
The age, occupation, disability and income of the claim petitioner were disputed.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts.A1 to A13 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No documentary evidence was produced by the respondents.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found n e g l i g e n c e o n t h e p a r t 2 0 2 5 : K E R : 7 4 4 4 1 M A C A N O . 8 3 1 O F 2 0 2 0 o f t h e f i r s t respondent/owner-cum-driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 5,76,250/- together with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of the petition till realization along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides 9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner - Notional income
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the latter, a 47-year-old homemaker as well as a fisher woman, was earning 15,000/- per month.

However, the Tribunal fixed the notional income at 5,000/-, which is quite low even going by the 2025:KER:74441 MACA NO. 831 OF 2020 dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Safiyath Beevi vs Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191207364/

sentences.text: Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the second respondent/insurer that if this Court is inclined to enhance the same, it may be as per the dictum in Ramachandrappa (Supra).
9.1. The claim petitioner herein is a 47-year-old lady who met with an accident resulting in amputation of her left limb below knee.
She is a homemaker also.
The fact that she is a fisher woman is not seen disputed.
That being the position, I find that an amount of 12,000/- to be just and reasonable amount, which can be fixed as the notional income of the claim petitioner.
Bystander expenses 10.
The accident took place on 23/10/2014.
The claim petitioner was hospitalized for a period of 35 days.
Therefore, I find that bystander expense at the rate of 350/- per day for a period of 35 days can be granted, which comes to 12,250/-.
Pain and suffering 11.
Though an amount of 2,00,000/- was claimed, the Tribunal has awarded an amount of 60,000/-.
As one of her limbs has been amputated, I find that an amount of 1,00,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
Percentage of disability 12.

The learned counsel for the claim petitioner submitted that 40% functional disability fixed by the Tribunal is on the lower side, especially when one of the limbs of the claim petitioner had to be amputated.

Per contra, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the second respondent/insurer that the percentage of disability that has been fixed by the Tribunal is quite reasonable and there are no other materials other than Ext.A13 which, for valid reasons, has not been accepted by the Tribunal.
Therefore, no infirmity has been committed by the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
12.1. As noticed by the Tribunal, Ext.A13 certificate itself says that it cannot be used for any medico-legal purpose.
Therefore, 2025:KER:74441 MACA NO. 831 OF 2020 the Tribunal was right in not relying on Ext.A13.
However, the fact that one of the limbs of the claim petitioner had to be amputated is not disputed by the second respondent/insurer.
Ext.A12 photos also make this fact evident.
That being the position, I find that the functional disability can be fixed as 50% in the facts and circumstances of the case.
Addition to be made towards future prospects 13.

As the claim petitioner was 47 years old and as the disability sustained is 50%, I find that 25% of her established income is liable to be added towards future prospects while computing compensation for permanent disability.
Extra nourishment 14.
Though an amount of 10,000/- was claimed, the Tribunal has awarded an amount of 5,250/-.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, compensation at the rate of 300/- for a period of 35 Safiyath Beevi vs Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191207364/
3 days can be granted, which comes to 10,500/-.
15.
